chapter: Venues, circuits and the music business
title: Arriving in New York and Central Park West
summary: She never dreamed of New York; she worked with Cab Calloway in the park and met the Rat Pack.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I came to New York to work. I didn't -- I never had to scrounge for a career. I never dreamed of coming to New York. It was the last thing on my mind.

I was living in Los Angeles. I never dreamed I'd come to Los Angeles, let alone New York, and I didn't know what New York was. I'd heard about it, I guess, but I got here and there were no trees and I thought I can't live here. It was weird to me. I was at the Wellington Hotel, and I was offered a job with Cab Calloway in the park, and for the first time I saw Central Park West and I knew I could stay here and that's where I met -- well, I knew them from Los Angeles. Sammy Davis, Frank Sinatra, the Rat Pack they called them. Wonderful men. Well, Duke Ellington was here and Louis Armstrong, everybody was here.
